text:
oliver: flagging a short proposal for an alternate reconnect flow - goal: reduce duplicate token generation and avoid cross-region hedging for transient disconnects. want quick feedback before i convert to RFC.

priya: nice. is this complementary to session leases or a replacement?

oliver: complementary. keep leases but shard them by tenant-namespace and use an owner-hint in the reconnect token so most resumes are local O(1) checks rather than global coord.

serge: owner-hint? explain briefly.

oliver: token encodes (shard_id, owner_node, short-hmac). on reconnect, the edge checks local shard; if owner_node matches and lease valid -> resume. otherwise fallback to existing multi-node reconcile.

laura: that reduces cross-node chatter. whats the expected false-positive/false-negative rate if owner node rotated?

oliver: rotation window small. we include a generation and ttl; if owner changed we fail fast and let the heavier path run. worst case is one extra full reconcile - no correctness loss.

priya: how many shards? static or adaptive?

oliver: start with 128 shards per region and autoscale based on active-session percent. shards map to sstable-like ring - cheap to compute.

serge: interesting. any memory cost numbers?

oliver: rough: 128 shards * ~2k entries active = ~256k entries. each entry ~120 bytes -> ~30MB per region. knobs available to reduce.

laura: how do we avoid hot shard allocation on noisy tenants?

oliver: reactive re-sharding: if shard load > threshold, we split it and reassign mappings. split ops are local and cheap. also backpressure noisy tenants via shard-level admission.

priya: what about hedging policy interactions? hedges currently don't carry reconnect tokens.

oliver: proposal: hedges copy current reconnect_token when spawned. upstreams race resume; owner-hint resolves locally so most hedges become no-ops quickly. if conflict, we surface a metric and short-circuit losing hedges.

serge: need to be careful about double-execution for side-effects. resume must be gated by route-level Resumable flag.

laura: +1 on Resumable flag. operator should default false for routes with external writes. add config: resumable_routes = {pattern: flags}.

oliver: we'll also add request-level idempotency tag for additional dedupe: X-Req-Id or X-Session-Gen. proxies set it if they may reattach.

priya: SDK impact?

oliver: optional. SDKs can surface reconnect_token for long polling. proxies will otherwise manage tokens. document header: X-Reconnect-Token and X-Resume-Owner-Hint.

laura: observability? we need clear tracing paths for resume wins vs fallbacks.

oliver: tracing: span attr session.resume=true/false, session.shard=<id>, session.owner_hit=true/false. metrics: resume_success_ratio, resume_conflict_rate, shard_splits.

serge: testing plan? fuzz with packet drops and leader rotations.

oliver: yes: 1) unit tests for token parsing and owner mismatch; 2) integration harness simulating TCP drops + node restart; 3) chaos run with 20% reconnects, verify no duplicate final outputs and <1% extra model token re-eval.

priya: rollout strategy? canary by region?

oliver: step rollout: start in non-prod, then 10% of prod by region, ramp with metrics gating (resume_conflict_rate, tail_latency). ops-bot will add a kill-switch config for immediate rollback.

ops-bot: note: gating hooks will be created in console. operator toggle: feature.toggle.ingress_resume_sharding.

laura: one operational concern: GC pressure from split shards. ensure background GC doesn't stop the fast-path.

oliver: GC will be incremental and capped CPU; we also expose shard.memory_pressure metric to auto-throttle.

serge: security: tokens include short-hmac; rotate hmac keys regularly. avoid logging tokens.

oliver: agreed. tokens are redacted by default in traces and logs. keys rotated weekly via keystore.

priya: looks reasonable. i'm curious about worst-case latency when owner mismatch hits fallback. estimated p99?

oliver: fallback path adds ~8-12ms control hop in-region, cross-region fallback more like 30-50ms. we'll tune heap sizes to avoid GC stutters.

laura: please add a migration note for Dedicated customers - they may want explicit shard counts and a migration tool.

oliver: will add dedicated migration document and admin CLI to export/import shard map.

priya: +1 to RFC. keep the initial proto minimal and list expansion points.

serge: +1. two asks in RFC: sequence diagrams for happy/failure paths, and a short operator playbook for rollback.

oliver: thanks - i'll draft and ping reviewers. example header snippet below for drafts: 

```
POST /v1/stream
Headers:
  X-Reconnect-Token: s_ghf7-<shard:42>:<owner:node-7>:<hmac>
  X-Req-Id: rq_12a
  Resumable: true
```

oliver: draft will include shard split flow and metrics dashboard workbook. pinging @laura @priya @serge for initial review. :thumbsup:
